#4 FIXED and verified. Root cause: `src/locale/nl.js` used a German-style ordinal `n => `${n}.``; Dutch day-of-month ordinals are `1ste, 2de, 3de, …, 8ste, 20ste, 21ste, 31ste`. Fix: `ordinal: n => `[${n}${n === 1 || n === 8 || n >= 20 ? 'ste' : 'de'}]`` (bracketed so the `s` isn't re-parsed as the seconds token). Verified `Do` for days 1–31 all correct, `npx jest` full suite: 56 suites / 524 tests pass, 0 failures. No pre-existing tests modified.

#5 FIXED and verified. Root cause: `src/plugin/weekYear/index.js` handled only the late-December case (week 1 → next year) and missed the reverse: with `yearStart: 4` (ISO-like weeks), early-January dates in week 52/53 belong to the previous year, but the plugin returned the calendar year (e.g. `dayjs('2021-01-01').locale('en-gb').weekYear()` gave 2021 instead of 2020). Fix (3 lines added): `if (month === 0 && weekOfYear >= 52) return year - 1`. Verified with an exhaustive 2010–2025 day-by-day sweep against reference week-year semantics (0 mismatches) plus the existing weekYear/weekOfYear/isoWeek tests; full suite `npx jest`: 56 suites / 524 tests pass, 0 failures.

#1 FIXED and verified. Root cause: `d.tz(input, timezone)` treated every input as a wall-clock string in the target zone, so timestamps / JS Dates / Day.js objects got shifted by the target offset (`dayjs.tz(1234567890123, 'America/New_York')` returned 23:31:30-05:00 instead of 18:31:30-05:00). Fix: non-string inputs are now converted to an instant first (`d(input).tz(timezone)`), and `proto.tz` keeps the instant exact (rounded offset minutes + preserved ms). Verified: all three input kinds now equal `dayjs(...).tz(...)` and the reference values; existing timezone tests 14/14 pass; full suite `npx jest`: 56 suites / 524 tests pass, 0 failures; also passes under TZ=Pacific/Auckland, Europe/London, America/Whitehorse.

#7 FIXED and verified. Root cause: the `A`/`a` meridiem tokens in `src/plugin/customParseFormat/index.js` were hard-coded to ASCII `/[AP]M/` and decided AM/PM by literal `=== 'PM'`, ignoring `locale.meridiem(...)` — so locale meridiem strings (zh-cn 上午/下午, ko 오전/오후, ja 午前/午後, br a.m./g.m.) never matched and parsing returned Invalid Date. Fix: tokens now use the generic word regex plus a `meridiemMatch` helper that inverts the locale's `meridiem(hour, minute, isLowerCase)` (falling back to the old English behaviour when a locale has no meridiem). Verified against reference values for zh-cn/ko/ja/br and default locale AM/PM plus lowercase `a`; `npx jest test/plugin/customParseFormat.test.js` 38/38 pass; full suite 56 suites / 524 tests pass, 0 failures.
